literal: Like slipping from a firm path is a slip of speech before those who accept and understand vast knowledge.
translation: Making a slip of speech before those who can receive and understand vast knowledge is like losing one's footing and falling from a safe path.
modern: பரந்த அறிவை ஏற்று ஆராயும் வல்லமை உடையவர்கள் முன்னிலையில், ஒருவர் பேசும்போது தவறு செய்வது என்பது, நல்ல வழியில் செல்லும்போது நிலை தடுமாறி விழுவதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the gravity of making a mistake when speaking before an audience of highly learned and discerning scholars. The poet compares a slip of tongue or an error in argument before such an audience to a traveler losing their footing and falling while walking on a well-established path. Just as a fall on a smooth path is highly embarrassing and damaging, an intellectual slip before those who truly understand vast subjects ruins one's reputation instantly. Therefore, one must be extremely careful and precise when speaking in front of wise people.
